text: Meet Ann.
This year, she got a two percent raise.
And prices? Didn't move. Zero inflation.
Now meet Barbara. She got five percent.
Nice. Except prices went up four percent.
So, who's better off?
It's Ann, right? Her pay buys two percent more stuff.
Barbara's buys about one.
In a famous study from 1997, seventy-one percent of people got that right.
Then a different group was asked who's happier.
Sixty-four percent said Barbara.
Barbara, meanwhile, is out celebrating with the shopping.
Which, of course, now costs four percent more.
That's the money illusion.
We read the number on the pay slip, not what it can buy.
And it's not just a quiz.
Between 2010 and 2025, the average wage in the UK rose fifty-two percent.
After prices? About three.
So, is your raise lying to you?
Let's check the receipts.
